stem: The “Big Bang Theory” is related to –
expl: The ''Big Bang Theory'' is related to the origin of the Universe, Milky Way and Solar System. This theory was propounded by Georges Lemaitre (1894-1966). Later in 1967, Robert Wagner explained this theory. According to this theory, the whole universe was concentrated in a hot and dense point some 13.7 or 13.8 billion years ago. Due to high concentration, there was a sudden explosion which was termed the Big-Bang.

stem: The ''Big-Bang Theory'' explains the origin of –
expl: The "Big Bang Theory" explains the origin of the universe from the earliest known period through its subsequent large scale evolution. The measurement of the expansion rate of the universe places this moment approximately 13.7 or 13.8 billion years ago, which is thus considered the age of the universe.

stem: The milky way is classified as –
expl: According to the theory propounded by Georges Lemaitre, 13.7 or 13.8 billion years ago the total cosmic substance was in the form of dense mass which spread to form a number of galaxies. An infinite group of these swirling galaxies is visible to us collectively in the form of the universe. Every galaxy is estimated to contain around 100 billion stars. The galaxy in which our solar system is situated is known as the ‘Milky Way’. There are various shapes of galaxies, for example elliptical, spiral, irregular etc. Spitzer Space Telescope in 2005, produced clear proof against the preconception about the shape of the Milky Way and made it clear that the shape of our Milky Way is barred spiral.

stem: Time taken by the Sun to revolve around the centre of our galaxy is –
expl: The Sun is one of the stars of our galaxy (Milky Way). Every star of the galaxy revolves around the galactic centre and the time taken by a star in revolving around this centre depends upon the distance between the galactic centre and the star. Sun is relatively far from the centre, so it takes more time to revolve around it. The Sun is at a 7.94 KPC or 25,896 thousand light years away from the centre and with a speed of 720 thousand km/hour, it takes 22.5 to 25 crore years, to revolve around the centre of the Milky Way galaxy. This period is called ‘Cosmic Year or Galactic Year’.

stem: The limit beyond which stars suffer internal collapse is called :
expl: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar was an Indo-American physicist who described the “Chandrasekhar Limit”. This limit describes the maximum mass of a white dwarf star or the mass limit above which a star will ultimately collapse into a neutron star or a black hole. He revealed that this mass was approximately 1.44 times of the solar mass. In 1983 Chandrasekhar was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on the evolution of stars.

stem: The 'Black Hole' was first made known by

He is known for the Chandrasekhar limit which showed that there is a maximum mass that is supported against gravity by pressure made up of electrons and atomic nuclei (the value of this limit is about 1.44 times of the solar mass) which was derived by Chandrasekhar. He was awarded Nobel Prize for Physics jointly with W.A. Fowler in 1983.

options.label: a

options.label: b

options.label: c

expl: Assertion (A) and Reason (R) both are true and Reason (R) explains Assertion (A) properly. It is not possible to observe a black hole directly with the help of a telescope. The intense gravitational field of a black hole due to the high density does not allow any type of radiation. Even light rays cannot escape from this. The presence of black hole is ascertained by the behaviour of stars, gases and masses near it with the help of space telescope.

stem: A 'Supernova' is –
expl: A supernova is a large explosion that takes place at the end of a star's life cycle. A supernova happens where there is a change in the core or center of a star. A change can occur in two different ways, with both resulting in a supernova. The first type of supernova happens in binary star systems wherein two stars orbit the same point. The second type of supernova occurs at the end of the a single star's lifetime.

stem: How many constellations are in our space?
expl: According to the International Astronomical Union, there are 88 constellations in the sky. Most of these imaginary patterns can be seen from the southern hemisphere. It will take a full year to get a glimpse of all the constellations.

stem: Which one of the following is not an Astronomical object?
expl: Brittle star is not an astronomical object. Brittle stars are echinoderms in the class Ophiuroidea closely related to starfish. These are aquatic creatures and crawl on the sea floor, while a Pulsar is a celestial body emitting very regular pulses of radio waves. A quasar is an astronomical object of very high luminosity found in the centers of some galaxies at a distance of billions of light-years. A black hole is also a cosmic body of extremely intense gravity from which nothing (even light) can escape and is formed by the death of a massive star. Thus, option (b) is the correct answer.

stem: Which one of the following is NOT found in space?
expl: Pulsar, Black Hole and Quasar are found in space while Brittle Star is an echinoderm closely related to Starfish. Hence Brittle Star is related to the sea, not space.

stem: Hubble space telescope has captured, for the first time, detailed image of the surface of a distant star. Name of the star :
expl: Betelgeuse is the second-brightest star in the constellation of Orion. It is at a distance of about 700 light years from the Earth. The Hubble Space Telescope obtained the first direct image of a star other than the Sun : betelgeuse.

stem:

expl: Due to the absence of atmosphere in space, the sky appears black and stars do not twinkle. stem: If the stars are seen to rise perpendicular to the horizon by an observer, he is located on the –
expl: Stars move parallel to the celestial equator around North and South celestial poles. The celestial North and South poles are straight overhead to the geographical North and South Poles and celestial equator is almost at overhead to the geographical Equator and at 900 to the Poles. It creates occlusion from the points of East and West at the horizon. The degrees of celestial poles are equal in number to latitude of the equator for the horizon. If an observer sees the stars perpendicular to the horizon he is located at the equator.
